focus: Compare the live qga socket against a temporary libvirt-managed unix virtio channel attached through virsh on the same running domain.
findings: A temporary libvirt-managed unix channel named `org.codex.libvirttest.0` attached successfully on the live domain and appeared as `channel2` on `port 3, guest off, host off`.

That temporary libvirt-managed channel created `/run/user/1000/libvirt/qemu/run/channel/1-regprobe-win11-25h2-/codex.libvirttest.sock`, and direct host-side AF_UNIX connect to that socket returned `CONNECT_OK`.
At the same moment, the live qga socket `/run/user/1000/libvirt/qemu/run/channel/1-regprobe-win11-25h2-/org.qemu.guest_agent.0` still returned `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`.
After detach, the temporary channel socket disappeared cleanly, while the live qga socket remained.
